1.B: Mature B-cell (Burkitt-type) neoplasms are TdT-negative and express surface immunoglobulin; TdT positivity marks an immature precursor blast.
1.C: Myeloid blasts express MPO, CD13, CD33 and CD117, not the B-lineage antigens CD19 and CD10.
1.D: T-lymphoblasts are defined by cytoplasmic CD3 (with CD7, CD5), not CD19 and CD10, which indicate B lineage.

2.A: B-ALL is defined by CD19, CD79a and CD22; cytoplasmic CD3 is the T-lineage-defining marker, and a mediastinal mass is typical of T-lineage disease.
2.C: AML blasts express myeloid markers such as MPO, CD13 and CD33; TdT with cytoplasmic CD3 indicates T-lymphoblasts.
2.D: Hodgkin lymphoma can cause a mediastinal mass but its Reed-Sternberg cells are CD30/CD15 positive, not TdT and cytoplasmic CD3 positive lymphoblasts.

3.A: BCR::ABL1 (Philadelphia chromosome) is a high-risk lesion in childhood ALL, managed with added tyrosine kinase inhibitor.
3.B: KMT2A rearrangement, typical of infant ALL, is an adverse-risk finding.
3.D: Hypodiploidy (especially fewer than 44 chromosomes) is adverse; it is high hyperdiploidy, not hypodiploidy, that is favourable.

4.A: Anti-CD20 therapy (rituximab) is used in mature B-cell lymphoma; it does not target the BCR::ABL1 kinase and is not used alone in Ph+ ALL.
4.B: FLT3 inhibitors target FLT3-mutated AML; BCR::ABL1 is inhibited by ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as imatinib or dasatinib.
4.C: Proteasome inhibitors (bortezomib) are used mainly in myeloma and some relapsed ALL protocols; they do not target the BCR::ABL1 fusion kinase.

5.B: Presenting leucocyte count is an initial NCI risk factor but not a response measure; treatment response is assessed by MRD.
5.C: Platelet count at diagnosis is not used for risk stratification and says nothing about response to therapy.
5.D: Liver span reflects organ infiltration at presentation and is not a quantitative response measure used for risk adaptation.

6.A: Renal infiltration may cause nephromegaly but does not explain headache and cranial nerve palsy.
6.C: Thyroid involvement is not a recognised sanctuary site and would not produce cranial nerve palsy.
6.D: Pericardial involvement causes effusion or tamponade, not headache and cranial neuropathy, which point to CNS leukaemia.

7.A: Ototoxicity is characteristic of platinum agents such as cisplatin, not asparaginase.
7.B: Haemorrhagic cystitis is caused by cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide (acrolein), prevented with mesna.
7.D: Pulmonary fibrosis is classically linked to bleomycin and busulfan, not asparaginase.

8.A: Cardiomyopathy is the dose-related toxicity of anthracyclines such as doxorubicin and daunorubicin.
8.B: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus is associated with ifosfamide tubulopathy (and lithium), not vincristine.
8.C: Pulmonary fibrosis is linked to bleomycin and busulfan; vincristine causes neuropathy, jaw pain, constipation and SIADH.

9.B: Peripheral neuropathy is the dose-limiting toxicity of vincristine, not anthracyclines.
9.C: Nephrolithiasis relates to urate in tumour lysis, not to cumulative anthracycline exposure.
9.D: Hypothyroidism follows neck or cranial irradiation; anthracycline surveillance targets cardiac function by echocardiography.

10.A: Mesna protects the bladder from cyclophosphamide/ifosfamide metabolites; it does not rescue methotrexate toxicity.
10.C: Dexrazoxane is a cardioprotectant used with anthracyclines and has no role in methotrexate rescue.
10.D: Allopurinol prevents uric acid formation in tumour lysis and does not reverse methotrexate antifolate toxicity.

11.A: B-ALL lymphoblasts lack Auer rods, which are fused MPO-positive primary granules found only in myeloid blasts.
11.B: T-ALL blasts are lymphoid and do not contain Auer rods.
11.D: CLL consists of mature small lymphocytes with smudge cells, not Auer rods, and is virtually absent in children.

12.A: Imatinib targets BCR::ABL1 in CML or Ph+ ALL; it has no activity against PML::RARA.
12.B: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 antibody for B-cell lymphomas and plays no role in APL.
12.C: Hydroxyurea only lowers counts; APL needs ATRA, which differentiates promyelocytes and rapidly corrects the coagulopathy.

13.B: Waiting for PML::RARA confirmation is dangerous; ATRA is started on morphological suspicion because early haemorrhagic death is the main risk.
13.C: Lumbar puncture is avoided during active APL coagulopathy because of bleeding risk and is not an initial priority.
13.D: Observation allows fatal bleeding; platelets, cryoprecipitate and FFP are given immediately with ATRA.

14.A: ETV6::RUNX1 is a favourable B-ALL fusion and is not a targeted-therapy marker in AML.
14.C: SMN1 deletion causes spinal muscular atrophy, not AML.
14.D: FMR1 CGG expansion causes fragile X syndrome and has no role in AML treatment.

15.A: RB1 mutations cause retinoblastoma, not Down-syndrome myeloid proliferation.
15.B: WT1 is linked to Wilms tumour and WAGR/Denys-Drash syndromes; TAM in trisomy 21 is driven by GATA1 mutation.
15.D: NF1 predisposes to JMML and other tumours but is not the defining lesion of transient abnormal myelopoiesis.

16.A: CD3 is a T-lineage marker and does not indicate megakaryoblasts.
16.B: CD19 and CD10 indicate precursor B-lymphoblasts.
16.C: CD30 and CD15 characterise Hodgkin Reed-Sternberg cells; megakaryoblasts express CD41 and CD61.

17.B: ESR is a nonspecific inflammatory marker and cannot assign lineage.
17.C: Serum ferritin reflects iron stores or inflammation and gives no lineage information.
17.D: Reticulocyte count reflects marrow erythroid output and cannot characterise blast lineage.

18.A: The Widal test is a serological test for typhoid and cannot classify leukaemia.
18.C: Serum IgE relates to atopy or parasitic infection and has no role in leukaemia classification.
18.D: Stool occult blood looks for GI blood loss and does not characterise blasts.

19.A: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma shows Reed-Sternberg cells in an inflammatory background, not a starry-sky pattern with MYC rearrangement.
19.B: Follicular lymphoma is rare in children and is linked to BCL2 t(14;18) with a follicular pattern, not MYC.
19.D: Lymphoblastic lymphoma may look starry-sky but is TdT-positive precursor disease without the defining MYC rearrangement.

20.A: Nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma usually presents with cervical or mediastinal nodes, not a rapidly growing jaw mass.
20.B: Langerhans cell histiocytosis causes lytic jaw lesions or floating teeth but grows slowly and has no endemic geography.
20.C: ALL without tissue disease presents with cytopenias and blasts, not a rapidly enlarging jaw mass.

21.B: Burkitt lymphoma presents with rapidly growing abdominal or jaw masses and starry-sky histology, not Reed-Sternberg cells.
21.C: AML presents with cytopenias and marrow blasts; Reed-Sternberg cells are not seen.
21.D: Lymphoblastic leukaemia shows marrow lymphoblasts and cytopenias, not Reed-Sternberg cells in a painless node.

22.A: CD3 and TdT mark T-lymphoblasts; Reed-Sternberg cells are TdT-negative and usually CD3-negative.
22.C: CD41 and CD61 are megakaryocytic markers used in acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia.
22.D: MPO and CD33 are myeloid markers for AML, not Hodgkin cells.

23.A: A mediastinal mass does not cause insulin deficiency; the anaesthetic risk is airway and vascular compression.
23.B: Acute liver failure is not a recognised biopsy risk here; the danger is loss of airway or venous return under sedation.
23.D: Contrast does not cause hypercalcaemia; the specific risk is cardiorespiratory collapse when sedation removes muscle tone.

24.A: Pruritus may occur in Hodgkin lymphoma but is not one of the staging B symptoms (fever, drenching night sweats, weight loss over 10%).
24.B: Mild rhinorrhoea is a trivial nonspecific symptom and not a B symptom.
24.C: Isolated constipation is not a B symptom; only fever, drenching night sweats and significant weight loss count.

25.B: LDH is released from any proliferating or dying cells and does not indicate B lineage.
25.C: LDH is not specific for CNS disease; CNS spread is shown by CSF cytology and imaging.
25.D: Raised LDH reflects disease burden; it signals more disease, not cure.

26.A: FNA alone loses tissue architecture and often gives too little material, so it is not adequate for every case.
26.C: Blood culture detects bacteraemia and cannot classify lymphoma.
26.D: Urine cytology has no role in lymphoma subclassification.

27.A: Waiting for a repeat blood count delays treatment of ECG-changing hyperkalaemia, which can cause arrhythmia at any moment.
27.B: Oral iron is irrelevant and adds nothing; the emergency is hyperkalaemia with ECG change.
27.D: Outpatient follow-up is unsafe; potassium 6.7 with QRS widening needs immediate calcium and potassium-lowering treatment.

28.A: SIADH causes hyponatraemia with concentrated urine, not high urate, phosphate and potassium with low calcium.
28.B: DKA causes hyperglycaemia, ketosis and metabolic acidosis; it does not produce hyperuricaemia and hyperphosphataemia after chemotherapy.
28.C: HUS causes microangiopathic haemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury; this post-chemotherapy electrolyte pattern is tumour lysis.

29.B: Rasburicase (urate oxidase) rapidly breaks down existing uric acid to allantoin, which is the opposite of what the stem describes.
29.C: Calcium gluconate stabilises the myocardium in hyperkalaemia and has no effect on uric acid.
29.D: Sodium bicarbonate alkalinisation is no longer recommended in TLS, and it does not reduce uric acid production.

30.A: Iron deficiency does not contraindicate rasburicase; the risk comes from the hydrogen peroxide it produces in G6PD deficiency.
30.C: Beta-thalassaemia trait does not impair the response to oxidant stress and is not a contraindication.
30.D: Mild eczema is not a contraindication to rasburicase.

31.A: Waiting for culture growth delays treatment; empiric antibiotics are given within about an hour of presentation.
31.B: Antihistamines do nothing for febrile neutropenia, which can progress quickly to sepsis.
31.D: Observing for 24 hours is unsafe with ANC 200/µL; febrile neutropenia needs immediate empiric antibiotics.

32.A: Iron deficiency anaemia causes microcytic anaemia without leucocytosis, hypoxia or neurological signs.
32.B: Viral lymphadenopathy does not cause hyperleukocytosis with hypoxia and neurological symptoms.
32.C: ITP causes isolated thrombocytopenia and bleeding, not leucocytosis with microvascular occlusion.

33.B: Mild splenomegaly has no effect on the airway or anaesthetic safety.
33.C: A small reactive neck node does not threaten the airway.
33.D: A renal cyst is incidental and irrelevant to anaesthetic risk.

34.A: Vincristine is neurotoxic and not ototoxic, and it does not raise lipase; ototoxicity belongs to platinum agents.
34.C: Anthracyclines cause cardiotoxicity, not cystitis, and neither explains acute pancreatitis.
34.D: Methotrexate causes mucositis, hepatotoxicity and crystal nephropathy, not acute pancreatitis with high lipase.

35.A: CD3 is expressed in both T-LBL and T-ALL, so it cannot separate them.
35.B: TdT is positive in both, as both are precursor lymphoblastic neoplasms.
35.D: Mediastinal masses occur in both; the conventional cut-off is marrow blasts of at least 25% for T-ALL.

36.A: ETV6::RUNX1 is a favourable-risk B-ALL lesion.
36.B: High hyperdiploidy (51-67 chromosomes) is favourable; it is low hypodiploidy that is adverse.
36.C: Rapid MRD clearance is a favourable response feature, not high-risk biology.

37.B: Prophylactic antibiotics prevent infection but have no anti-leukaemic effect in the CNS sanctuary.
37.C: Platelet transfusion is supportive and does not reduce CNS relapse.
37.D: G-CSF speeds neutrophil recovery but does not treat CNS leukaemia.

38.A: BCR::ABL1 defines CML and Ph+ ALL, not APL.
38.C: ETV6::RUNX1 is a favourable fusion in B-ALL.
38.D: MYC::IGH t(8;14) is the hallmark of Burkitt lymphoma.

39.A: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma usually presents with cervical or mediastinal nodes in adolescents, not bulky abdominal disease with a very high proliferative index.
39.B: CML presents with marked leucocytosis and splenomegaly, not a bulky high-proliferation abdominal mass.
39.D: Follicular lymphoma is rare in children and is indolent rather than very highly proliferative.

40.A: Pneumothorax is an acute line-insertion complication with respiratory symptoms, not limb swelling.
40.B: Tumour lysis is a metabolic syndrome early in therapy and does not cause unilateral limb swelling.
40.C: Nephrotic syndrome causes generalised oedema; new limb swelling with a catheter and asparaginase points to venous thrombosis.
